solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bond accepting kiss over death

indicators.note: in an across clue, turning a word over flips its letter order end to end
a word accepting something takes it inside itself

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link
X is the cross for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: James Bond gets a kiss just before a death scene in a spy film.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE takes in X to make TIXE, which read backwards is EXIT. 'Bond' looks like 007 but is just a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit is a euphemism for dying, as in making one's final exit from life's stage.

clue.text: Stray cat yelled, on and off, up tree

indicators.note: to stray is to wander from order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: on and off means alternately taking and skipping letters

parts.note: letters one, three and five
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stray cat, yowling intermittently, has climbed up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like the cat's position, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypt is the general name for a eucalyptus, the gum tree of Australia.

clue.text: It blocks connection to sailor at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all eight letters used

explanation.surface: Something at sea cuts a sailor's link to the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolator is a switch or insulator that breaks or blocks an electrical connection.

clue.text: Hack journalist wearing jacket pondered

indicators.note: what is wearing a jacket sits inside it, so the jacket goes round the other letters

parts.note: a book's jacket is its cover
to hack is to hew or chop
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A hack reporter in a jacket sat thinking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack journalist' reads as one phrase, a poor writer, but splits into a verb and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew something over is an idiom for thinking it through at length.

clue.text: US artist coming from hotel, half-improved

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word's letters are kept

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to enrich something is to improve it

explanation.surface: An American painter emerges from a hotel looking somewhat better.
explanation.walkthrough: The first four of ENRICHED's eight letters follow H.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Henri was an American painter, leader of the Ashcan School of early twentieth-century realism.

clue.text: Booze on account of which wind audibly delivered

indicators.note: something delivered audibly is spoken, so it is judged by sound

parts.note: why means for what reason
to twine is to wind round

explanation.surface: Drink is to blame for someone breaking wind loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, WHY TWINE runs together as the name of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: White wine is an alcoholic drink, and booze is slang for any alcohol.

clue.text: Pig after spitting into big cup — clean ones may be found here

definitions.text: clean ones may be found here

indicators.note: into puts these words inside the cup letters

parts.note: DD is a large bra cup size

indicators.note: after places the pig word behind the weather word

parts.note: it is spitting when light rain falls
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A pig is spitting into a large cup, and clean ones sit nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ones' refers back to cups: freshly washed cups and plates are left on the board to drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A draining board is the ridged surface beside a sink where clean dishes are left to dry.

clue.text: When blotto, even I'd streaked

indicators.note: blotto means very drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: all six letters used

explanation.surface: Someone admits that, drunk enough, even they would have run naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaked' suggests running naked, but it means marked with lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Veined marble or leaves are marked with lines or streaks of colour.

clue.text: Double Gloucester in germ-free packs

indicators.note: the phrase packs the answer inside it, spanning its words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Double Gloucester cheese wrapped in sterile packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double Gloucester' is a famous English cheese, so the definition is welded onto the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringer is someone who looks exactly like another person, usually as a dead ringer.

clue.text: Sing softly outside yard in London borough

indicators.note: the singing word sits outside, wrapping round the other part

parts.note: to croon is to sing in a soft low voice
YD is the standard abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Someone sings quietly out in a garden in a London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Croydon is a large borough in south London, best known for its town centre and tram network.

clue.text: Decline to reorient aid after redistribution

indicators.note: redistribution hands the letters out again in a different arrangement

parts.note: all thirteen letters used

explanation.surface: Economic decline prompts a rethink of where foreign aid goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb, refuse, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterioration is a decline, a gradual worsening in condition or quality.

clue.text: Asian queen visiting Paisley?

indicators.note: a visitor goes into someone's place, so one word is put inside another

parts.note: Ian Paisley was the Northern Irish Protestant politician and preacher
a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: A queen from Asia goes to visit Paisley, the Scottish town famed for its patterned fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Paisley poses as the Scottish town (or the fabric pattern) but stands for Ian Paisley, giving IAN, which wraps round RANI.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iranian comes from Iran, a country in western Asia, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: In US, however, contract covers most of unforeseen development

indicators.note: a word that covers another goes round it

parts.note: a lease is a rental contract

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is used

parts.note: a twist is a plot development nobody saw coming

explanation.surface: A contract has clauses for most unexpected developments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In US' tells you the word is American usage; 'however' alone would never suggest it in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is an American informal adverb meaning at least, or anyway, used much like however.

clue.text: Church with oddly naïve leading girl

indicators.note: leading puts the selected letters in front of the church abbreviation
oddly means take the letters in the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An innocent young girl leads the way into church.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a girl relative, a sibling's daughter; girl is a loose but fair stand-in.

clue.text: Monstrous female in jail having delayed second series

indicators.note: in places the monster inside the jail word
delaying a letter takes it out of its place in the word so it can arrive later, at the end

parts.note: a prison is a jail
an ogress is a female ogre
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A monstrous woman in prison has had her second hearing postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delayed' moves the jail word's S to the very end, behind everything else, rather than dropping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Progressions are ordered sequences, like a series of numbers or chords following on from one another.

clue.text: Hospital's cashiers, stuck up type

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: in a down clue, sticking something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cashier someone is to dismiss them, so cashiers means fires

explanation.surface: Snooty hospital cashiers are a stuck-up type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashiers' looks like a noun for till staff, but it is the verb, dismisses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans serif is a typeface without the small finishing strokes on letters, so a kind of type.

clue.text: Artist at home turned up wearing boy's cords

indicators.note: the reversed part is worn by the boys, so it goes inside them

parts.note: lads are boys; the 's is read as is

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up makes the letters read upwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: An artist turns up at home wearing a boy's corduroy trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cords' looks like corduroys, but it means ropes. The answer is a less common spelling of lanyards.
explanation.definitionFit: Laniards (lanyards) are short cords, such as those used on ships or to hang a whistle round the neck.

clue.text: King Lear's half confused with three daughters, primarily

indicators.note: half means only two of the four letters are used
confused letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: the first half of the king's name
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter only is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: King Lear goes half mad over his three daughters.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear, in Shakespeare, has three daughters, which makes 'King Lear' look like the definition; the king is another one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred was the name of several Anglo-Saxon kings, notably Ethelred the Unready.

clue.text: Table an expletive in strong denunciation

parts.note: a counter is a shop or kitchen table
blast is a mild curse

explanation.surface: Someone tables a swear word in a fierce telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' looks like a verb, as in table a motion, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterblast is a vigorous written or spoken attack replying to an earlier one.

clue.text: One in two records makes conclusion in Boston

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the two records

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record and a log is a written record
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One musician's work on two records forms the finale of a Boston concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Boston' signals the American spelling, without the final -ue.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilog (British epilogue) is a concluding section added at the end of a book or play.

clue.text: Cover you might put on slate area above dam?

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means placed before the following piece

parts.note: to slate or pan is to criticise harshly
A is the abbreviation for area
a dam is an animal's mother, and ma is mother

explanation.surface: A builder puts slate on a roof over a reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a roof covering, and 'dam' a reservoir wall, but dam is a mother here.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a straw hat, a head covering you put on.

clue.text: Old fashion designer back from trip given by London academy

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London

explanation.surface: An ageing designer returns from a journey to give a talk at a London academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario Prada founded the Italian fashion house in 1913, so he is an old fashion designer.

clue.text: Extended watch captures cuckoos in tree

indicators.note: capturing something holds it inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to stare is to watch for a long time
anis are tropical American birds of the cuckoo family

explanation.surface: A long vigil by a birdwatcher pays off with cuckoos spotted in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoos' tempts as an anagram signal, but anis are actual cuckoos.
explanation.definitionFit: Star anise is a small evergreen Chinese tree whose star-shaped fruit is used as a spice.

clue.text: Try stopping horse being docked in old marketplace

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the word sits inside the other
docking cuts off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop a horse having its tail docked in an ancient market.
explanation.walkthrough: ARAB loses its last letter to give ARA, which takes in GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square and marketplace of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Fancy earl bringing in king that is more likely to let things through?

definitions.text: more likely to let things through?

indicators.note: bringing something in puts it inside
fancy means elaborate or made up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
K is the chess abbreviation for king
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dandy earl welcomes the king to a court where secrets slip out.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters LEAR open up for K and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A leakier container lets more through its holes, and the question mark admits the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Terrible error consuming gutted dance instructor

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are scrambled
consuming something takes it inside

parts.note: the five letters rearranged

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dance teacher, devastated, makes a dreadful mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted dance instructor' reads as a heartbroken teacher, but gutted works on dance alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderer gives orders, so is one who instructs or commands.

clue.text: Self-contained residence in New York and Florida covered by conveyance

indicators.note: what is covered by something lies underneath, inside it

parts.note: a grant is a legal conveyance of property
the state's abbreviation
Fla. is the traditional abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: A self-contained home in New York and Florida is conveyed in a property deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyance' looks like a vehicle but is the legal transfer of property.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny flat is a self-contained annexe or apartment for an elderly relative, often in or beside a family home.

clue.text: Employed head of Washington Post, for example

parts.note: the paper is American, so US describes it
a newspaper's head is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: Someone was given a job running the Washington Post.
explanation.walkthrough: The Washington Post's head is a US editor, a US ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Employed and used both mean put to work or made use of.
